correctness.rationale: The source proves a concrete stronger statement than fixed-exponent counterexamples. In E_odd, conditional expectation in the prime-2 Bohr coordinate contracts every H^p norm for p>=1; the cofinal p_j=2-1/j (j>=2) form a complete Frechet topology, so each neighborhood is controlled by one p_j. For D_X(s)=sum_{n<=X}n^{-s}, Harper Theorem 1 gives ||D_X||_{H^p} = O_p(sqrt(X)/(loglog X)^{1/4}) for fixed 1<=p<2. The odd projection B_X=D_X-2^{-s} D_floor(X/2) obeys the exact parity identity and ||B_X||<=||D_X||. Euler summation uniformly for 1/2<=sigma<=3/4, |t|<=T gives B_X(s)=X^{1-s}/(2(1-s))+O_T(1). At eps_X=1/log X this yields inf_{|t|<=T}|B_X(1/2+eps_X+it)| >=c_T sqrt(X), hence the normalized block grows at least (loglog X)^{1/4}; imaginary translations preserve norms. Adding a sufficiently small scaled B_X to an odd Dirichlet polynomial proves density of each open set U_(I,k,m) requiring modulus >k uniformly on rational-ended I at some 0<eps<1/m. Baire yields simultaneous dense G_delta uniform limsup blowup on all compact positive-length intervals. For fixed nonzero F in this residual set, prime sets of F and G(2^{-s}) are disjoint, so Haar-product Fubini gives exact H^p norm factorization for all 0<p<2; positivity of F norm makes T_F an injective topological embedding of the complete Frechet disk Hardy intersection with closed infinite-dimensional range. Finally a nonzero analytic G has modulus bounded away from zero on a smaller subarc of |z|=2^{-1/2}; multiplying by the uniformly unbounded F on that subarc forces each nonzero image function to have unbounded limsup of local log-plus integrals. All interval, exponent, and limsup quantifiers are respected. Independently recomputed odd-block Euler errors at X=1000,10000,60000 with t in [-6,6] (49 grid points): 1.30842,1.31917,1.32455 maximum, respectively, and checked independent-variable p-moment factorization with 2048-point circle grid at p=1.5,1.8,1.99 to error <=2.3e-16. These finite tests do not prove Harper, the Baire argument, or any infinite claim; those rely on the reconstructed analytic steps and cited original theorem.

value.rationale: The subcritical local Nevanlinna obstruction is a natural boundary question at the sharp p=2 threshold. The result distinguishes exceptional examples from stable geometry: one F works in every H^p, p<2, has uniform approach blowup on every compact boundary segment, and multiplication by disjoint-prime disk functions yields a CLOSED infinite-dimensional space ALL of whose nonzero members inherit nowhere-local failure. A norm-factorized embedding is an independently useful structural fact, not merely a minor estimate, textbook renaming, or arbitrary finite slice. The result is precise and naturally motivated, while limited to nonconstructive Baire existence and limsup approaches.
